title: Debye shielding
caption: Mobile electrons and ions crowd round any charge in a plasma and cancel its field beyond a few Debye lengths: φ ∝ e^(−r/λ_D)/r instead of 1/r. At one Debye length the potential is already down to 1/e (0.37) of the bare Coulomb value; at three, to 0.05.
alt: Potential against distance in Debye lengths: the bare Coulomb 1 over r curve and a shielded curve that falls much faster and is nearly zero beyond 3 Debye lengths.
description: Distance r in units of the Debye length λ_D; potential in units of q/(4πε₀λ_D).
Shielded: φ = e^(−r)/r, 0.368 of the bare value at r = λ_D and 0.05 at 3λ_D.
So a plasma looks neutral on scales much larger than λ_D: that is one of the conditions for calling a gas a plasma.
